questions.question: Process the four year-end adjustments and state where each leftover piece stands on the statement of financial position.
questions.expected_answer: Depreciation R8 900: vehicle 20% straight-line on cost R40 000 = R8 000; equipment 10% diminishing balance on carrying value R9 000 (10 000 − 1 000) = R900; accumulated depreciation grows, no cash moves. Accrued expense: water and electricity 2 400 + 400 = R2 800 expense; R400 a current liability. Prepaid expense: insurance 1 800 − 300 = R1 500 expense; R300 a current asset. Accrued income: rent 5 500 + 500 = R6 000 income (12 months at R500); R500 a current asset. Each adjustment corrects the year figure by matching and parks the difference on the statement of financial position.

questions.question: Build net profit and prove the statement of financial position balances.
questions.expected_answer: Trading: sales 120 000 − cost of sales 80 000 = gross profit R40 000 (50% mark-up on cost). Profit and loss: 40 000 + rent income 6 000 − expenses 31 200 (wages 18 000, water and electricity 2 800, insurance 1 500, depreciation 8 900) = net profit R14 800. Equity: 70 000 + 14 800 − drawings 6 800 = R78 000. Assets: non-current at carrying value 70 300 (land and buildings 38 200; vehicles 40 000 − 16 000; equipment 10 000 − 1 900) plus current 15 400 (stock 8 000, debtors 4 500, bank 2 100, prepaid 300, accrued income 500) = R85 700, equal to equity 78 000 plus current liabilities 7 700 (creditors 7 300 + accrued expense 400).

questions.question: Compute and comment on the year's key indicators, then give the unit cost and budget arithmetic.
questions.expected_answer: Gross profit on cost 40 000/80 000 = 50%, matching the policy, so no unrecorded stock leakage; on sales 33,3%. Net profit on sales 14 800/120 000 = 12,3%. Current ratio 15 400/7 700 = 2 : 1, comfortable; acid test 7 400/7 700 = 0,96 : 1, just under one to one, worth watching. Solvency: assets cover liabilities about eleven times. Return on equity 14 800/74 000 average = 20%, several times bank savings rates — worth the effort and risk. Every comment: figure, comparison, judgement. Unit cost: (6 000 + 4 000 + 2 000)/1 000 = R12; at R15 selling price, R3 per unit. Budget: receipts 9 000 − payments 7 500 = surplus 1 500 + opening 1 000 = closing R2 500, cash-only rules observed.
